instruction.text: Let’s learn about seasons at the North and South Pole.

feedback.finish: The poles are the northernmost and southernmost points on Earth.
Both poles tilt so far towards the sun in their summers, that it stays light for 6 months!

atoms.b: In this image, it is ((++summer winter)) at the South Pole.

instruction.text: Select the moon to find out about winter at the poles.

correct.text: Winters at the poles last for 6 months, and it stays completely dark. Temperatures at the South Pole can get as cold as -90°C!
correct.sound: Winters at the poles lasts for 6 months, and it stays completely dark. Temperatures at the South Pole can get as cold as minus ninety degrees Celsius.

atoms.a: At the South Pole, it is always light during the summer.
During the summer, the North Pole is completely dark.
During the winter, temperatures at the South Pole are normally about 30°C.
